rows.evidence: Q1: Methods Sections 2.1-2.3 and Results Sections 3.1-3.3 report the authors' own comparison of OpenET-based irrigation calculations with farmer records (239 field-years) and WIMAS flowmeter data at field, water right group and management area scales (Tables 1-3, Figs. 3-8).
rows.notes: The study does not report any result of its own on water savings produced by data-supported enforcement of the SD-6 LEMA pumping reduction. The 20% allocation, the 26-31% reduction in withdrawals and slowed water-table decline are cited from other work (Drysdale and Hendricks 2018; Deines et al. 2019; Butler et al. 2020; Whittemore et al. 2023) in Section 2.1.2 as background for site selection. The LEMA enforcement rests on totalizing flowmeters, not on remotely sensed ET; the study only evaluates whether remotely sensed ET can estimate irrigation withdrawals/applications (bias 1.6-4.9% at field scale, positive bias at WRG and management-area scales) and explicitly concludes that uncertainties among ET models exceed the signal of conservation measures in the region. This is a precondition (measurement capability) for data-driven regulation, not evidence of the conservation effect.

rows.evidence: Q1: Methods Sections 2.1-2.3 and Results Sections 3.1-3.3 report the authors' own comparison of OpenET-based irrigation calculations with farmer records and WIMAS flowmeter data at three spatial scales (Tables 1-3, Figs. 3-8).
rows.notes: The study reports no data of its own on crop yield or productivity. The statement that the LEMA had only minor negative impacts on yield and none on profitability is cited from Golden (2018) in Section 2.1.2 as background. The study's own results concern the accuracy of remotely sensed ET for calculating irrigation water use, which at most supports a precondition for data-driven regulation, not its effect on yields.

notes: Full text available including references; supplementary figures (S1-S6) not included but not needed for rating. The study is a primary validation of ET-based irrigation estimation against metered records; it does not itself assess the LEMA's water savings or yield outcomes, and remotely sensed ET was not part of the LEMA enforcement mechanism described.
